verdict.summary: Self-serve with no review: create the app, set distribution to 'Any workspace', and any Asana user with your authorize link can connect the same day. The required config is distribution plus scopes: granular scopes don't cover every endpoint yet, so some agents fall back to Full permissions, and Enterprise admins can approve or block your app per organization.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app in the developer console, pick scopes, add an HTTPS redirect URL, and run the code flow. Development needs an HTTPS redirect (self-signed or a tunnel) because the docs don't mention localhost.

timeToProd.assumes: An OAuth app shared to Any workspace that reads and writes tasks and projects; an app directory listing is optional and adds an unspecified review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: No review needed. Per customer: Enterprise admins approving the app where they manage apps from the admin console.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The distribution page describes no review for Specific or Any workspace sharing.

prerequisites.item: An Asana account in a workspace you belong to
prerequisites.why: Apps are created in the developer console while signed in, and Specific-workspace distribution uses workspaces you belong to.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URL (or urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob for native/CLI apps)
prerequisites.why: Non-native apps must use an https redirect URL.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs suggest a self-signed certificate or stunnel for local development.

prerequisites.item: For an app directory listing: company page URL, support URL or email, test credentials, and a listing that follows the guidelines
prerequisites.why: Incomplete listings delay publication and can trigger extra review cycles.

scopeTiers.impact: Sign-in only; request id_token via response_type.
Lets an agent read tasks, projects and comments with least privilege. Read, write and delete don't imply each other.
For agents that create tasks, comment or register webhooks. Subsequent authorizations aren't additive, so always request the full set.
Access to all endpoints, including ones without granular scopes yet. Broader consent, which may make Enterprise admins less likely to approve.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The admin-approval effect is our inference.

steps.title: Create the app in the developer console
steps.detail: Sign in, open My apps > Create new app, enter the name and purpose.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: app.asana.com/0/my-apps returned 302 to the login page on 2026-10-20; we did not sign in.

steps.title: Choose scopes
steps.detail: Map each endpoint the agent calls to a granular scope (e.g. tasks:read, stories:write). Use Full permissions only if a needed endpoint has no scope yet.

steps.title: Configure redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: On the OAuth tab add the HTTPS redirect URL, tick the scopes (or Full permissions), and copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Implement the code flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256&scope=tasks:read%20projects:read. Exchange at POST https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_token. With Full permissions, omit scope or send scope=default.

steps.title: Handle token refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens last one hour (expires_in 3600). Refresh with the refresh token, which keeps working as long as the user keeps the app authorized. Use /-/oauth_revoke on disconnect.

steps.title: Add rate-limit and concurrency handling
steps.detail: Plan for 150 requests/min per token on free domains and 1,500 on paid, 60 searches/min, 50 concurrent GETs and 15 concurrent writes, plus cost-based limits. Always honor Retry-After.

steps.title: Set distribution to Any workspace
steps.detail: Under Manage distribution choose Any workspace so users outside your workspaces can authorize. Sharing settings can only be changed while the app is unpublished.

steps.title: Prepare material for Enterprise admins
steps.detail: Write clear listing details (what the app does, scopes used, data handling), since Enterprise admins review them to approve or block apps.

steps.title: Optional: submit to the app directory
steps.detail: Use Submit for review in the console, complete the pre-flight checklist and listing, and provide test credentials. The app is locked for edits while in review.

steps.title: Optional: app directory review
steps.detail: Asana emails when the app is ready to publish or needs changes. Apps with app components also get a security review and QA. No timeline is published.

agentCanDo: Map endpoints to granular scopes and decide whether Full permissions is needed
Implement the PKCE code flow, refresh and revoke
Add Retry-After, concurrency and cost-aware throttling
Draft the listing details Enterprise admins review
Prepare app directory listing copy and the pre-flight checklist
humanMustDo: Sign in to the developer console and create the app
Set the redirect URL, scopes and distribution to Any workspace
Provide reviewer test credentials and submit to the app directory, if listing

blockers.symptom: Users outside your workspace can't authorize the app
blockers.cause: Distribution is set to Specific workspaces.
blockers.fix: Switch distribution to Any workspace in the developer console (only possible while unpublished).

blockers.symptom: forbidden_scopes error on the authorize request
blockers.cause: The request includes scopes not registered for the app, or specific scopes while Full permissions is on.
blockers.fix: Register the scopes in the console, or with Full permissions omit scope / send scope=default.

blockers.symptom: Calls to some endpoints are forbidden even with granular scopes
blockers.cause: Scopes aren't yet available for every Asana API endpoint.
blockers.fix: Enable Full permissions for those endpoints, or avoid them.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error returned isn't documented on the page we read.

blockers.symptom: Lost permissions after a second authorization
blockers.cause: Scope requests aren't additive; a later request with fewer scopes replaces the earlier grant.
blockers.fix: Always request the full set of scopes the agent needs.

blockers.symptom: Enterprise users can't use the app
blockers.cause: Their admin manages apps from the admin console and hasn't approved yours, or blocked it.
blockers.fix: The customer's admin approves it; give them clear listing details.

blockers.cause: Free domains allow 150 requests/min per token, plus concurrency and cost limits.
blockers.fix: Honor Retry-After, request fewer fields with opt_fields, and use webhooks instead of polling.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: opt_fields advice is our inference from the cost-based limit.

nuances.text: Access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens don't have a stated expiry and keep working while the user keeps the app authorized.
Rejected requests still count against the quota, so retrying before Retry-After makes throttling worse.
Switching distribution from Any to Specific workspace blocks new authorizations from outside users, and published apps can't change sharing settings.
Asana marks the scope list as 'subject to revision', so re-check it when adding endpoints.
Asana doesn't serve an OIDC discovery document at app.asana.com/.well-known/openid-configuration, although the authorize endpoint accepts id_token response types.
